title: To Kill a Mockingbird
synopsis: Maycomb, Alabama, summer. You are Scout. Your father, Atticus, will be defending a Black man no Maycomb jury wants acquitted. Don't shoot a mockingbird.

nodes.text: Jem, Dill, the tire swing. You run barefoot.

choices.consequence: “Play” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Joy.
You commit to “Watch the street.” The story records the instinct as “Honest” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Dare him out, Jem says. The house is closed up.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Touch the door.” The story records the instinct as “Brave” and carries it forward.
You commit to “Stay on the sidewalk.” The story records the instinct as “Wise” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: She corrects you. She loves you. She is, you realize, the household's spine.

choices.consequence: “Listen” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honor.
“Push back” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Spirit.

nodes.text: Miss Caroline tells you not to read. You stop.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Survive.
There is no taking “Argue” back. Spirit shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: He stands up. He sits down. He tells you to climb into someone's skin.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Honor.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Honest.

nodes.text: A man accused. Atticus accepts the case.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Honor.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Honest.

nodes.text: A crowd. Atticus reads under a lamp. You step out.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Brave—follows you into whatever comes next.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Wise—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: The colored balcony. Reverend Sykes makes room.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honor—follows you into whatever comes next.
There is no taking “Sit on the lawn” back. Honest shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Atticus, gentle, takes apart Mayella's story.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Honor.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honest—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: He says he felt sorry for her. The courtroom shifts.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Note the moment.” The story records the instinct as “Honor” and carries it forward.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Witness.

nodes.text: Atticus speaks of equality. The room is silent.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Honor.
“Sit” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honor.

nodes.text: Guilty.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Don't cry in the balcony” back. Discipline shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
“Cry” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honest.

nodes.text: She tells you a lady doesn't act like that.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Spirit—follows you into whatever comes next.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Civil.

nodes.text: Tom is shot. The town is, for a moment, ashamed.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Mourn” back. Honor shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
There is no taking “Hate” back. Honest shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: You are a ham. The school is dark.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Wear it” back. Joy shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You commit to “Refuse it.” The story records the instinct as “Pride” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Footsteps behind. Bob Ewell.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Survive—follows you into whatever comes next.
“Freeze” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honest.

nodes.text: A man you don't see carries Jem home.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Care.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honest—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Boo Radley, finally, in your house. White skin, soft voice.

choices.consequence: “Smile” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honor.
“Stare” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honest.

nodes.text: You walk Boo home. You stand on his porch and look at the street through his eyes.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Look long.” The story records the instinct as “Wise” and carries it forward.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honest—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: He reads to Jem. He stays.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Safe—follows you into whatever comes next.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Honor.

nodes.text: You grow up. Maycomb does, slowly, change. The county school, eventually, is a different building.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Stay” back. Roots shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Forward.
Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: You become a writer. You publish a small careful book about a town you loved and didn't. The book becomes the way many people learn what you learned.
You become a lawyer. You take, eventually, your father's office. The desk is the same. The work is harder than he made it look.
You stay in Maycomb. You teach school. You sit, sometimes, on Boo's old porch. The town heals slowly. So do you.
